RUN THE SUITE ONLY UNDER THE GUARD. Before any pytest run, install an independently enforced outbound-network denial with connection-attempt logging: every non-loopback name resolution and connect is refused, each attempt is recorded (test, target, outcome) and fails the test that made it by name, even when the code under test catches the error. Attempted connections are reported separately from completed connections. Do not test hermeticity by allowing real requests and seeing whether they happen.

PLACEHOLDERS WIN. From before the first autornd import, the suite's configuration belongs to the suite: every model tier (required and optional), the provider key, provider order, provider fallbacks and every credential setting are forced (not setdefault) to a placeholder or empty value that no export and no .env in the working directory can displace, and the suite does not read the dotenv file (a setting in autornd/config.py, said so here per 112's allowance). A test that needs a different value sets it itself.

RULING FIRST, VERBATIM, in HANDOVER.md and the notebook, before the repair code in commit order. The ruling text is the owner's: 'Missing or whitespace-only assessment is not completed verification. An implementation explicitly marked incomplete cannot qualify for completed delivery. Unavailable verification is distinct from passing verification.' Record it under the next unused ruling ID — D49, because D47 and D48 are claimed by the unexecuted commands 113 and 114 and were never committed, and one ID must not name two rulings. Apply it narrowly, on typed fields, never prose parsing, preserving the distinctions among failed, unchecked, unavailable and passed checks.

RESERVATIONS ARE OWNED. Each dispatch's reservation is identified, and only the call that made it releases it, on reconciliation or on failure. A call that reserved nothing (blind, or no ceiling set) releases nothing; so does a test double that books cost without guarding. A failed call keeps its OWN worst case as unreconciled liability. The call ceiling counts every call in flight, blind ones included. One reservation per call stands, held across that call's retries.

PRICING IS HONEST. An absent prompt or completion price in the catalogue makes the model unrated (the guard's blind list, recorded), never a zero rate; an explicit catalogue zero stays a priced zero; a published per-request charge is added to the worst case. Explicit zero pricing must be distinguishable from missing pricing, provider-free.

THE COMPLETED TERMINAL MEANS FINISHED. A run whose final implement verdict is explicitly done=false ends blocked, naming the incomplete implementation. A validation verdict whose evidence is missing, empty or whitespace-only resolves red with a cause naming what was absent, counted like every normalization.

A SKIPPED CHECK SAYS SO. The doublecheck skip output is {'skipped': True, 'vetoed': False, 'reason': ...} with no ship; DoubleCheckVerdict gains the computed property vetoed (equal to not ship — a property, not a field, so the schema and the model's output are unchanged); independent_verdict's condition reads independent_check.vetoed == false in both workflow files, so the gate reads the same typed path on both branches. A check that ran and said do-not-ship still ends the run blocked with its findings.

EVERY TERMINAL RECONCILES. Every terminal path of the API engine writes the client's booked spend into the workflow row, including paid retries followed by failure, and records outstanding liability separately from booked spend (one additive nullable column through the existing _add_missing_columns pattern; the eval unit record already carries both).

PROVE EVERY REPAIR. A reproduction test that fails on the current code, quoted; a regression test that passes after; and each repair proved by breaking one line and quoting the failure. For every existing test a repair changes, say which of the two is wrong (convention 17).
